erin: Quick sync: we hit two surprising behaviors during the staging run for the multi-mode handshake. Need to converge on manifest fields + runtime state transitions.

noah: Observed: hosted issued an ephemeral delegate token, Private immediately rejected due to policy. Meanwhile KV reads succeeded on cached entries -> leak of stale state.

yasmin: I'd like a tiny manifest extension: cred_behavior (pass-through|delegate|require-rebind), cache_policy (flush|isolate|keep), and fallback_behavior (service-principal|forward-creds). Example below.

erin: Can you paste a short example?

yasmin: Yep:
```yaml
handshake:
  src: hosted
  dst: private
  cred_behavior: require-rebind
  cache_policy: isolate
  fallback_behavior: service-principal
  audit: detailed
```

noah: For cache_policy=isolate semantics: runtime should create a new cache namespace for the new binder and mark old namespace as quiescing. Reads from old namespace are allowed until TTL, writes go to new namespace. This prevents instant eviction races.

yasmin: Agree. Also add cache_epoch header so any client can detect which cache namespace it's reading from and reject stale indexes.

erin: On fallback_behavior, prefer service-principal to avoid exposing tenant KMS credentials in hosted. But we must include a tenant_shim_id so telemetry attributes cost back to the tenant.

infra-bot: infra-bot: smoke test "handshake-epoch-probe" passed on staging-rt at 03:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

noah: Edgecase: if Private returns "require-rebind" but client already has in-flight tokens, we need a REBIND_GRACE period. Propose states: ACTIVE -> QUIESCE(inflight-grace) -> AWAIT_REBIND -> BOUND. Expose metrics: handshake_state and handshake_duration.

yasmin: Also add audit events: handshake.request, handshake.bind_succeeded, handshake.bind_refused(reason), cache.epoch_changed(old->new), fallback.invoked(method). Each event should include correlation_id and tenant_id.

erin: Action items: yasmin will update the manifest draft with defaults (cred_behavior: delegate -> deny by default? maybe default require-rebind for safest), noah will draft state-machine diagram and metric names, i'll add telemetry mapping for service-principal fallbacks. We'll roll this into RFC-112 follow-up.

yasmin: I'll also prototype the cache_epoch header in the client SDK so we can detect stale reads server-side.

erin: Cool. if we keep defaults conservative we can loosen later after perf tests. Thanks all :thumbsup:
